questions.passageHtml: Pollination syndromes are suites of floral traits that have independently evolved as a result of selection pressure exerted by pollinators; melittophilous (bee-pollinated) flowers, for example, frequently exhibit a fresh, mild scent. questions.stemHtml: What does the text most strongly suggest about the study conducted by Rosas-Guerrero et al.?

choices.label: A
choices.html: A limitation in the methodology used by the researchers may entail that the study’s conclusion is not well supported.

choices.label: B
choices.html: Because the study contained data on a limited number of plant species, its conclusion is accurate for those species but cannot be applied to species not in the study.

choices.label: C
choices.html: Due to the difficulty of gathering representative research on angiosperms, the study may have included previous research with a focus too heterogeneous to be comparable.

choices.label: D

questions.passageHtml: Neuroscientist Artin Arshamian and his team sought to determine what affects a person's perception of an odor as pleasant: is it culture, personal taste, or aspects of human anatomy? choices.label: B

choices.label: C
choices.html: people from the Malay Peninsula tended to rate linalool as more pleasant than mushroom alcohol regardless of differences in their anatomical characteristics or personal tastes.

choices.label: D
choices.html: people from the Malay Peninsula and people from Ecuador tended to rate more odors as pleasant than as unpleasant.

questions.passageHtml: Mariana Lopes Barata and Pedro Simões Coelho collected data from 324 music-streaming service users to identify factors that influence users to opt for paid (premium) versions of music streaming services, like Apple Music. questions.passageHtml: Animals use many objects as tools to achieve goals more easily. Such goals include grooming, finding food, and protecting themselves. questions.passageHtml:
Text 1

Kikko (tortoiseshell) and other Japanese sashiko embroidery patterns use motifs drawn from nature and daily activities, classic sources of inspiration in folk-art traditions. A category that resists firm delineation, folk art is generally defined by an intimate connection to quotidian life. “The beauty of such objects,” writes Sōetsu Yanagi in The Unknown Craftsman, “is not so much of the noble, the huge, or the lofty as a beauty of the warm and familiar.”

Text 2

Through their beautiful handmade aesthetic, painting and textiles from Japan’s twentieth-century mingei (folk art) movement represent an unambiguous rejection of mass-produced consumer goods. At the same time, mingei, properly considered, stands apart from fine art, as its rootedness in commonplace craft traditions gives it an authenticity and accessibility that fine art, with its prizing of sophistication and innovation, cannot match.
questions.stemHtml: Which choice best describes how Text 1 differs from Text 2?

choices.label: A
choices.html: Both texts highlight the principally utilitarian nature of folk-art objects, but Text 1 acknowledges a complementary decorative function that is not mentioned in Text 2.

choices.label: B
choices.html: Text 1 suggests that the nature-based aesthetic of folk art is inherently resistant to change, while Text 2 implies that the pressures of consumer culture have indirectly altered how folk art is made.

choices.label: C
choices.html: Text 1 identifies characteristics shared by folk art across cultural contexts, while Text 2 describes how a universal characteristic of folk art is manifest within a specific tradition.

choices.label: D
choices.html: Both texts valorize folk-art traditions, but Text 1 does so by emphasizing qualities that are intrinsic to folk art, whereas Text 2 makes reference to other modes of cultural production.

  • Researchers detected magma by tracking earthquake waves that slowed down when passing through chambers of magma consisting of 3% to 32% melted rock.

  • These findings challenge the scientific theory that magma chambers only exist right before eruptions.
  • The discovery could improve volcano monitoring and eruption prediction methods.
questions.stemHtml: A student wants to undermine a scientific assumption about magma chambers. Which choice most effectively uses relevant information from the notes to accomplish this goal?

choices.label: A
choices.html: Researchers detected magma chambers by tracking earthquake waves through partially melted rock, improving volcano monitoring and eruption prediction methods for dormant volcanoes.

choices.label: B
choices.html: By tracking earthquake waves, Pang found that magma reservoirs sit 3 to 9 miles below the Cascade Range volcanoes’ surface and need over 35% liquid magma to potentially erupt.

choices.label: C
choices.html: Magma chambers need over 35% liquid rock to potentially erupt, refuting the assumption that volcanoes dormant for thousands of years have melted rock below.

choices.label: D
choices.html: Scientists found inactive Cascade Range volcanoes with large magma chambers below their surface, challenging the theory that magma chambers only exist right before eruptions.

While researching a topic, a student has taken the following notes:

While researching a topic, a student has taken the following notes:

¢ It consists primarily of journal entries written by a teenager living in an apocalyptic society.

Sanchez-Sanchez and colleagues employed a conductivity, temperature, and depth (CTD) profiler to remeasure the depth of the TJBH. choices.html: the narrator states, “The four travelers passed through the rest of the forest in safety, and when they came out from its gloom saw before them a steep hill, covered from top to bottom with great pieces of rock.”

choices.label: B
choices.html: a character says to Dorothy, “I cannot understand why you should wish to leave this beautiful country and go back to the dry, gray place you call Kansas.”

choices.label: C

questions.passageHtml: When the first railroads were built in Australia in the 1800s, a variety of track sizes (gauges) were used across the continent, resulting in what historians call the "railway gauge muddle.” The Dreamworld Railway line in Queensland used narrow tracks. ______ the Mornington Railway line in Victoria used broad gauge tracks.

questions.passageHtml: Emulsification is a process that creates a uniform mixture that includes two ingredients that do not combine on their own, such as oil and water. For this process to happen, a third ingredient, an emulsifier, must be combined with the other two. Carrageenan, a substance extracted from red seaweed, is a common emulsifier: it helps to create a smooth texture in yogurt that makes it more pleasant to eat.
questions.stemHtml: According to the text, what result is associated with carrageenan?

choices.label: A
choices.html: It prolongs the time it takes for ingredients to mix together during the making of yogurt.

choices.label: B
choices.html: It assists in the evaporation of water during the making of yogurt.

choices.label: C
choices.html: It helps ensure that yogurt has a smooth texture.

choices.label: D
choices.html: It decreases the amount of one ingredient in yogurt while increasing the amount of another.

questions.passageHtml:
While researching a topic, a student has taken the following notes:

  • Researchers Gwangsu Kim et al. sought to explore the relationship between the brain's ability to process natural sounds and its ability to process music.
  • They used an artificial deep neural network (DNN) that models how the brain processes auditory information. ¢ The DNN had been trained to detect natural sounds (excluding music).
  • Finding: The DNN spontaneously developed neurons that responded to music but not to other auditory stimuli.
  • Conclusion: The brain's ability to process music may arise as a by-product of natural sound processing.
questions.stemHtml: The student wants to present the aim of the study. Which choice most effectively uses relevant information from the notes to accomplish this goal?

choices.label: A
choices.html: By training an artificial deep neural network, the researchers aimed to establish that the brain’s ability to process natural sounds arises as a by-product of processing music.

choices.label: B
choices.html: The researchers used an artificial deep neural network, which spontaneously developed neurons that responded to music but not to other auditory stimuli.

choices.label: C
choices.html: Using an artificial deep neural network, the researchers sought to explore the relationship between the brain’s ability to process natural sounds and its ability to process music.

choices.label: D
choices.html: In their study, the researchers evaluated whether an artificial deep neural network could model how the brain processes auditory information.

questions.passageHtml:
While researching a topic, a student has taken the following notes:

  • In a 2004 study, researchers Jorge E. Lopez and C. Vaughan wanted to explore the effects of ingestion by bats on the germination of Piper sancti-felicis seeds in Costa Rica.
  • The team of researchers tested 125 Piper sancti-felicis seeds that had been ingested by chestnut short-tailed bats.
  • Of these, 82 seeds (66%) germinated.
  • As a control, J.E. Lopez and C. Vaughan tested 125 Piper sancti-felicis seeds that had not been ingested by chestnut short-tailed bats.
  • Of these, 88 seeds (70%) germinated.
questions.stemHtml: The student wants to describe the study’s research methodology. Which choice most effectively uses relevant information from the notes to accomplish this goal?

choices.label: A
choices.html: The team of researchers tested the germination of 125 Piper sancti-felicis seeds that had been ingested by chestnut short-tailed bats and 125 Piper sancti-felicis seeds that had not been ingested.

choices.label: B
choices.html: Research by J.E. Lopez and C. Vaughan revealed that 82 of 125—that is, 66%—of the Piper sancti-felicis seeds that had been ingested by the bats germinated.

choices.label: C
choices.html: J.E. Lopez and C. Vaughan wanted to explore the effects of chestnut short-tailed bats’ ingestion on Piper sancti-felicis seed germination.

choices.label: D
choices.html: In the study, a lower percentage of Piper sancti-felicis seeds ingested by bats germinated than those that had not been ingested by bats.

questions.passageHtml:
While researching a topic, a student has taken the following notes:

  • Maya Lin is an American artist known for her memorials and works of installation art.
  • She completed the Civil Rights Memorial in 1989.
  • It is a memorial sculpture consisting of a fourteen-ton granite fountain, and it is designed to commemorate figures of the Civil Rights Movement.
  • She completed Avalanche in 1998.
  • It is an installation composed of glass that fills an entire gallery wall.
questions.stemHtml: The student wants to describe Avalanche to a new audience. Which choice most effectively uses relevant information from the notes to accomplish this goal?

choices.label: A
choices.html: Maya Lin's Civil Rights Memorial is a granite memorial sculpture that commemorates figures of the Civil Rights Movement, while Avalanche is an installation artwork.

choices.label: B
choices.html: Though Maya Lin's Avalanche (1998) is not a memorial, its gallery-filling scale may call to mind the imposing Civil Rights Memorial, which consists of a fourteen-ton granite fountain.

choices.label: C
choices.html: Artist Maya Lin is well known for her installation art, such as Avalanche (1998), and for her memorials.

choices.label: D
choices.html: Completed in 1998, Maya Lin's Avalanche is a large-scale installation artwork composed of glass that fills an entire gallery wall.
